newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crude steady on thin Dec supply, US arb.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crude steady on thin Dec supply, US arb.

text.p: North Sea crudes were steady in Thursday afternoon trade, underpinned by a thin supply of unsold December barrels and a gaping arbitrage to the U.S. but activity on paper and wet markets was thin, traders said.
Brent paper spreads were broadly unchanged from early levels with Dec/Jan talked at +82/+86 cents and Jan/Feb at +72/+77.

CFDs were talked firmer, with next week's dates trading at Jan Brent +38 cents for half a cargo, after a Dec 22-24 Brent sold at Jan +47 cents on Wednesday to a Wall Street trader collecting barrels for a transatlantic trip.
The following week also edged higher, talked about five cents firmer at Jan Brent +5/+9.

Jan Brent paper was notionally firmer with the IPE futures contract, which added 22 cents to $24.00 a barrel by 1606 GMT, led higher by a French oil workers' strike and a fire at a Louisiana refinery which boosted product prices.

Traders said only one Brent cargo, scheduled to load Dec 20-22, was due to turn wet on Thursday. Other unsold December supply was restricted to a couple of cargoes each of Gullfaks A and Ekofisk and one cargo each of Troll and Draugen.
U.K. Forties was also "well placed", traders said.

In the Mediterranean, traders were divided on the direction of Urals. Some expected the market to stay at recent firm levels, with supply disruptions at Novorossiisk expected to hold back barrels from the December loading programme.
"It's not going to come off," said one trader who was offering a Dec 12-13 loader at Dated Brent -5 cents.
But others said weakening refining margins on sour crude had softened demand for Urals at current high prices.
"Sweet grades are better for (Med) refiners at the moment," said one dealer for a trading house. "I think every (Urals) cargo will be a different case, but I'd bet on it going lower."
A Med refiner said that West African grades were offering a margin of 50/60 cents a barrel above Urals. He expected Urals to weaken to a discount of 40/50 cents below Dated Brent.
Bonny Light was particularly well bid, traders said.
Up to four end-Dec Bonny Lights were available. One seller was offering a cargo in the high 60s (cents) over Dated Brent with buying interest seen in the mid-60s.

Two Forcados were also up for grabs, talked in the +70s, as well as one Brass River and two Qua Iboes. A Qua Iboe cargo already on the water was traded at Dated Brent +36/38 but this was seen not representative of the late Dec market.
Most buying interest was seen from the Med, but arbitrage to the U.S. was also an option. Around six VLCCs of December-loading West African crudes was fixed to Asian markets, traders said.
-- Mark Thompson, Rosalind Russell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
